Definition: strengthened for a primary ἔδω (to eat); used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by G5315; to eat (usually literal):--devour, eat, live.
BiblicalUsage: Esthíō means to eat — the ordinary verb for taking food. Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners; the disciples eat the bread He breaks; and Paul warns that the way we eat can build up or destroy a brother. It is the commonest act of life, and Scripture treats it as a spiritual matter.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe esthíō dignifies the table: eating together is fellowship, and eating carelessly is a sin against a brother. I hold that the Lord's Supper is the proof — the meal is where the gospel is tasted.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; The Calling of Matthew
